lines.l0: Here’s how to set up Avorythm, in eight quick steps.
lines.l1: Step one. On the Chrome Web Store, click {add|Add to Chrome}, then {pin^pin it} to your toolbar. Edge works too.
lines.l2: Step two. In Google AI Studio, {create^create a free API key}, and {copy^copy it}.
lines.l3b: {paste^Paste the key} under {connect|Connect to Gemini}, and press {save|Save}. It stays in your browser.
lines.l3c: Then {tick^tick the consent box} for Google Gemini.
lines.l4a: Step four. On any video, {icon^click the Avorythm icon} and {pick^pick your language}. There are {n79^seventy-nine}.
lines.l4b: {onpage|On this page} is the fastest. The {sync|Synchronized recorder & player} adds pause, seek and export.
lines.l5: Step five. Press {start|Start translating}, and the video {speaks^speaks your language}.
lines.l6a: Step six. Switch each output on or off: {o1^original audio}, {o2^dubbed audio}, and {o3^both subtitles}.
lines.l6b: {card^Subtitles sit} on a frosted-glass card. {drag^Drag it anywhere}, and {resize^resize it}.
lines.l6c: {balance^Balance the original} against the dub, and {duck^smart ducking} lowers it while the dub speaks.
lines.l7a: Step seven. The synchronized player lets you {pause^pause}, {seek^seek}, and {full^go fullscreen}.
lines.l7b: Then {export^export} a WebM video with SRT subtitles.
lines.l8a: Step eight. The desktop app translates {any^any program}, on {os^Windows}, macOS and Linux.
lines.l8b: In {studio|File studio}, {drop^drop in a file}, and get all four outputs in {zip^one ZIP}.
lines.l9: Avorythm is {free^free and open source}. If it helps you, {star^give it a star} on GitHub.
